subject.title: fix(browser): use public ssrf runtime import in CDP proxy bypass

question: Should the managed-proxy CDP bypass helper stay on the private owner-scoped `ssrf-runtime-internal` path, or be promoted into the public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/ssrf-runtime` contract?
rationale: The current PR only changes one Browser import, but the correct repair crosses the Plugin SDK security boundary and sibling Ollama/Browser packaged-load behavior; automation should not choose that permanent SDK contract.

options.title: Preserve Private Owner-Scoped Helper
options.body: Repair packaged Browser/Ollama resolution while keeping managed-proxy bypass helpers private to the existing owner-scoped paths.

options.title: Approve Public SSRF Runtime Export
options.body: Promote the helper into public `ssrf-runtime` only with explicit SDK/security docs, guardrail updates, and compatibility proof.

options.title: Pick A Canonical Sibling PR
options.body: Close or pause this PR if maintainers prefer a sibling replacement such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96649, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96928, or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96994.

recommendation.title: Preserve Private Owner-Scoped Helper
recommendation.body: Repair packaged Browser/Ollama resolution while keeping managed-proxy bypass helpers private to the existing owner-scoped paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The open question is primarily package/export boundary policy, and steipete has recent private SDK declaration and package-boundary history in this area.
